title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor — Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low (P0532-v4)
shortDescription: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor fault: pressure sensor a circuit low. Stored as P0532-v4.
fullDescription: The HVAC control module monitors A/C refrigerant pressure to protect the compressor and engage the cooling fan. Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low indicates a circuit or rationality fault that can disable the compressor and stop cabin cooling. Compressor cycling and head-pressure protection rely on this sensor.
safetyImpact: Driveable; loss of cabin cooling and possible compressor damage.

causes.cause: Wiring or connector fault at sensor

symptoms: Cooling fan stays on or off

fixSteps.title: Check Refrigerant Charge
fixSteps.instruction: Connect manifold gauges and verify static and operating pressures.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Sensor Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect connector at the high-side pressure transducer for corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor Signal
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe sensor and check 5V reference, ground, and signal under varying pressure.

fixSteps.title: Replace Pressure Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Most pressure sensors thread into a Schrader-style port and can be changed without recovery.

faq.a: Often the system disables the compressor as a safety measure when the sensor fails.
Yes — only A/C function is affected, not engine drivability.

title: A/C Clutch Relay — Clutch Relay Control Circuit (P0645-v3)
shortDescription: A/C compressor clutch relay control fault: clutch relay control circuit. Stored as P0645-v3.
fullDescription: The PCM controls the A/C compressor clutch via a relay. Clutch Relay Control Circuit indicates a circuit fault — open coil, shorted driver, or stuck contacts — that prevents proper compressor cycling. Misbehaving clutch relays can cause continuous compressor operation and battery drain.
safetyImpact: Driveable; A/C may be inoperative or stuck on.

causes.cause: Wiring fault from PCM to relay

fixSteps.title: Swap Relay With Identical
fixSteps.instruction: Most fuse boxes contain identical relays — swap with horn or fan and retest.

fixSteps.title: Test Relay Coil & Contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Bench-test the relay with 12V on the coil and continuity across contacts.

fixSteps.title: Check Driver Signal
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe the PCM control wire and verify it pulls to ground when A/C is requested.

fixSteps.title: Replace Relay or Repair Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the relay or repair wiring as needed.

faq.a: Yes — most are plug-in style in the underhood fuse box.
If the relay sticks closed it can keep the compressor engaged and drain the battery.

title: Climate Control Module — Sensor Reference Voltage C Circuit High
shortDescription: HVAC climate control module communication or actuator fault: sensor reference voltage c circuit high.
fullDescription: The climate control module manages blend doors, blower, and compressor. Sensor Reference Voltage C Circuit High indicates an internal module fault, lost communication, or actuator out-of-range. Symptoms range from stuck temperature to inoperative HVAC display.
safetyImpact: No drivability impact; comfort/defrost only.

fixSteps.title: Cycle Ignition
fixSteps.instruction: Turn ignition off, wait 60 seconds, and restart to attempt module reset.

fixSteps.title: Scan All Modules
fixSteps.instruction: Use full-system scan tool to check for U-codes pointing at HVAC bus issue.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect HVAC harness connector behind glove box for corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Replace HVAC Module
fixSteps.instruction: If module fails self-test, replace and program with OEM tool.

faq.q: Can I just drive without A/C?
faq.a: Yes — climate faults rarely affect drivability.
Often a low battery during start corrupts module memory. Always replace a weak battery first.

title: Blend Door Actuator — Blend Door Actuator Driver Side Stuck
shortDescription: HVAC blend / mode door actuator fault: blend door actuator driver side stuck.
fullDescription: Blend door actuators position the temperature blend or air mode flap. Blend Door Actuator Driver Side Stuck typically appears as a clicking noise behind the dash and a stuck temperature or vent direction. Most actuators are plastic-geared and fail at the gear teeth.
safetyImpact: No drivability impact; cabin comfort only.

fixSteps.title: Listen for Clicking
fixSteps.instruction: Change temp setting and listen behind dash to localize the failed actuator.

fixSteps.title: Run Actuator Recalibration
fixSteps.instruction: Many vehicles support an actuator recalibration via scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Remove & Inspect Actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the actuator (typically 2-3 screws) and inspect gear teeth.

fixSteps.title: Replace Actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Install new actuator and run recalibration.

faq.a: Usually no — most actuators are under $80 and reachable without dash removal.
Stripped gears slip past the position stop, causing the motor to free-spin and click.

title: Blend Door Actuator — Mode Door Actuator Stuck
shortDescription: HVAC blend / mode door actuator fault: mode door actuator stuck.
fullDescription: Blend door actuators position the temperature blend or air mode flap. Mode Door Actuator Stuck typically appears as a clicking noise behind the dash and a stuck temperature or vent direction. Most actuators are plastic-geared and fail at the gear teeth.
safetyImpact: No drivability impact; cabin comfort only.

fixSteps.title: Listen for Clicking
fixSteps.instruction: Change temp setting and listen behind dash to localize the failed actuator.

fixSteps.title: Run Actuator Recalibration
fixSteps.instruction: Many vehicles support an actuator recalibration via scan tool.

title: Hybrid/EV Traction Battery Cooling — Battery Cooling Fan Control Circuit (P0AB0-v2)
shortDescription: Hybrid/EV traction battery thermal management fault: battery cooling fan control circuit. Stored as P0AB0-v2.
fullDescription: The Battery Energy Control Module (BECM) monitors traction-battery temperatures and runs a cooling fan or coolant pump. Battery Cooling Fan Control Circuit indicates the cooling system cannot maintain commanded temperature, which limits charge/discharge rates and can disable propulsion in extreme cases.
safetyImpact: Drive with caution; reduced power and possible battery damage.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Cooling Vent / Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Many EV/hybrid packs draw cabin air through a filter — inspect and clean.

fixSteps.title: Test Cooling Fan/Pump
fixSteps.instruction: Command fan or coolant pump via scan tool and confirm operation.

fixSteps.title: Check Coolant Level
fixSteps.instruction: On liquid-cooled packs, check coolant level at the battery reservoir (not engine).

fixSteps.title: Replace Fan/Pump or Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace failed component; some require dealer programming.

faq.a: The vehicle will derate power to protect the pack — drive gently to a service location.
Yes if ignored — heat is the #1 enemy of lithium-ion cells.
